SELECT cls, count(*) n_trips, sum(anglers) angler_days, sum(yt) yt_sum,
  round(sum(yt)/sum(anglers),4) ypa
FROM trips
WHERE fished_date_season=2 AND fished_date_doy BETWEEN 91 AND 121
GROUP BY cls ORDER BY ypa DESC

SELECT cls, boat, count(*) n_trips, sum(anglers) angler_days, sum(yt) yt_sum,
  round(sum(yt)/sum(anglers),4) ypa, max(fished_date_doy) last_doy
FROM trips
WHERE fished_date_season=2 AND fished_date_doy BETWEEN 91 AND 121
  AND cls IN ('three_quarter','day_1_5','overnight')
GROUP BY cls, boat HAVING sum(anglers)>=15
ORDER BY ypa DESC LIMIT 25

SELECT cls,
  CASE WHEN fished_date_doy<101 THEN '91-100' WHEN fished_date_doy<111 THEN '101-110' ELSE '111-121' END bin,
  count(*) n, sum(anglers) ang, sum(yt) yt, round(sum(yt)/sum(anglers),4) ypa
FROM trips
WHERE fished_date_season=2 AND fished_date_doy BETWEEN 91 AND 121
  AND cls IN ('three_quarter','day_1_5','overnight')
GROUP BY cls, bin ORDER BY cls, bin

import pandas as pd
trips = tables['trips']
fishdope = tables['fishdope']
climate = tables['climate']

def pooled_ypa(df, classes, season, doy_lo, doy_hi):
    sub = df[(df.cls.isin(classes)) & (df.fished_date_season==season) & (df.fished_date_doy>=doy_lo) & (df.fished_date_doy<doy_hi)]
    if sub.anglers.sum()==0: return (0.0, int(sub.anglers.sum()), len(sub))
    return (round(sub.yt.sum()/sub.anglers.sum(),3), int(sub.anglers.sum()), len(sub))

classes = ['three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5']

out = []
# season2 recent bins doy90-121
for lo in range(90,121,10):
    out.append(('S2', lo, lo+10, pooled_ypa(trips, classes, 2, lo, lo+10)))
# season1 doy120-320 in 20-day bins to find trough/fall pickup calendar
for lo in range(120,320,20):
    out.append(('S1', lo, lo+20, pooled_ypa(trips, classes, 1, lo, lo+20)))

# ONI last readings
oni = climate[climate.index_id=='oni'].sort_values('avail_t').tail(6)[['avail_season','avail_doy','value']]

# fishdope last 14 days (season2)
fd = fishdope[(fishdope.report_date_season==2)].sort_values('report_date_doy').tail(14)[['report_date_doy','yt_local','yt_coronado','yt_all','yt_local_catch']]

# pier temp season2 recent vs season1 same doy
pier = tables['pier']
def avg_temp(season, doy_lo, doy_hi):
    sub = pier[(pier.ts_season==season)&(pier.ts_doy>=doy_lo)&(pier.ts_doy<doy_hi)]
    return round(sub.wtmp_c.mean(),2)

temp_cmp = [(lo, avg_temp(1,lo,lo+10), avg_temp(2,lo,lo+10)) for lo in range(100,125,10)]

result = {'ypa_bins': out, 'oni': oni.to_dict('records'), 'fishdope_recent': fd.to_dict('records'), 'temp_cmp': temp_cmp}

import pandas as pd
trips = tables['trips']

def by_class(df, season, doy_lo, doy_hi):
    sub = df[(df.fished_date_season==season) & (df.fished_date_doy>=doy_lo) & (df.fished_date_doy<doy_hi) & (df.cls.isin(['three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5','full_day']))]
    g = sub.groupby('cls').agg(yt=('yt','sum'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), n=('yt','size'))
    g['ypa'] = (g.yt/g.anglers).round(3)
    return g

r1 = by_class(trips, 1, 120, 180)
r2 = by_class(trips, 2, 90, 122)

# check S2 latest individual trips in the 120-130 bin (why ypa=0)
recent = trips[(trips.fished_date_season==2)&(trips.fished_date_doy>=113)&(trips.cls.isin(['three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5']))].sort_values('fished_date_doy')[['cls','boat','fished_date_doy','yt','anglers']]

result = {'S1_120_180_by_class': r1.to_dict('index'), 'S2_90_122_by_class': r2.to_dict('index'), 'S2_recent_trips': recent.to_dict('records')}

# dope_solo notes — living doc. Read top section first (current plan), history below.

## CURRENT PLAN — as of Season 2, day 121 planning turn (21:00)
Status: $1550/$2000, 10/10 PTO, season score 0.0244 (3 probes: d100 hit 0.024,
d107 zero, d113 zero). Fully intact resources, no rush — good position.

**MAJOR UPDATE this turn: doy120-180 is NOT a trough — it's season 1's
SECOND-BEST window of the year, and we are in it right now.**
- Re-pulled season-1 ypa by class for doy120-180 (previously I only had a vague
  "moderate 130-180" note): **overnight 0.496 ypa (n=90), three_quarter 0.467
  (n=225), day_1_5 0.239 (n=39)**. Only the narrow fall peak (doy280-300,
  ypa 1.735) beats this. My old "TROUGH 180-260" label is correct for AFTER
  doy180, not for the 120-180 window we're now in through day 121.
- **Overnight was the best class in this window in S1, not three_quarter.**
  All three of my probes so far have been three_quarter only. Widen watching
  (and any future probe) to overnight too, not just 3Q.
- Season 2 status in this window (doy90-122 by class): three_quarter ypa 0.065
  (n=78), overnight 0.011 (n=17, essentially dead), day_1_5 0.15 (n=8, but
  driven almost entirely by one outlier: Pacific Voyager 24/24 anglers on
  doy113 — no other boat before/since corroborated it, treat as noise same as
  the d106/d112 three_quarter blips that didn't hold).
- **Water temp gap has closed/reversed**: S1 vs S2 avg pier wtmp_c at same doy
  — doy100: 16.42 vs 16.30 (close), doy110: 16.34 vs 16.68 (S2 warmer!),
  doy120: 15.90 vs 16.50 (S2 warmer!). The cold-water story from earlier in
  the season no longer explains flat counts.
- **ONI recovering steadily**: -1.57 (doy9) → -1.48 (doy40) → -1.29 (doy71) →
  -1.06 (doy99). Still cold/La Niña but trend is consistently warming, ~0.5
  per 90 days. Not yet at S1's level at the same point but closing.
- **Conclusion: temp/ONI no longer explain the gap, but the fleet-wide bite
  still hasn't shown up (S2 ypa ~7x lower than S1 in this window).** Something
  else (bait, structure, timing lag) may be holding it back, or it could still
  break any day. This is a genuine watch window, not a foregone bust and not
  a confirmed bite — stay disciplined on the trigger.

**Decision for the nightly self, next ~4-6 weeks (doy 121-165ish):**
1. Keep the existing trigger discipline: do NOT book on a single boat's
   one-day spike (proven trap 3x this season — d106, d112 three_quarter,
   d113 Pacific Voyager day_1_5 all reverted). Require either (a) trailing
   3-day pooled ypa on the SAME boat >0.2 with at least 2 non-zero trips, or
   (b) 2+ different boats in the same class both posting >0.15 ypa on
   overlapping days.
2. **Watch overnight class as hard as three_quarter now** — check
   `ctx.scheduled_boats('OVERNIGHT', day)` and recent overnight counts every
   night, not just 3Q. If overnight breaks the trigger, it's historically the
   stronger vehicle in this window (0.496 vs 0.467 ypa in S1) and also frees
   up PTO-free weekend testing same as 3Q (Fri departure = 0 PTO).
3. Keep testing cheap ($150 three_quarter, weekend/no-PTO) when the trigger
   fires, same as before — it's working as a low-cost probe (1 hit / 3 tries).
4. If a real multi-boat/multi-day breakout confirms (ypa sustainably >0.3-0.4
   across several boats for 3+ days), escalate to overnight ($400) or day_1_5
   ($550) and start committing PTO for weekday departures (remember 14-day
   lead time on CommitPTO) — don't wait for weekends only once it's real,
   since S1's 120-180 window ran for ~8 weeks, not just a few weekend windows.
5. If nothing confirms by ~doy165-170 (i.e. this window ends up a bust despite
   temp/ONI catching up), fall back to the standing plan: preserve budget/PTO
   for the fall peak, start watching fall signal by doy ~220-230 (a bit
   earlier than last plan's 230, since ONI recovery could pull the peak
   earlier than S1's doy280-300 too — re-check ONI print due ~doy130).
6. Don't forget classes never worth booking regardless of signal: HD_AM,
   HD_PM, TWILIGHT — confirmed dead for YT all of S1 and all of S2 so far
   (ypa ~0.00-0.01 every window checked, multiple times).

**Next planning turn checks:**
- Re-pull three_quarter AND overnight pooled ypa for doy121-current (daily),
  see if either broke the trigger and held for 3+ days.
- Re-check ONI (next print ~doy130) and pier temp gap — is S2 still tracking
  even with/ahead of S1, or falling back cold?
- If a bite confirmed and I escalated, note which specific boats performed
  best (boat-level variance still unanalyzed — do it once there's a live
  signal window with real counts to compare boats on).
- Leaderboard oddity: several agents (weekender, thrifty_solo, tides,
  follower, skeptic_solo, greenwater) show season_fish=0.6117 with strategy
  "books nothing" — looks like placeholder/seed data, not real competition.
  Don't over-react to it; watch if it changes to real numbers next turn.

---

## Season-1 baseline reference (revised)
- Half-day/twilight classes are dead for YT all year (ypa ~0.00-0.01). Never
  book them.
- Season 1 calendar by class-pooled ypa (three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5):
  doy90-100 spike ~0.86 (overnight 1.8-2.8 alone); doy100-120 dip; **doy120-180
  strong second window: overnight 0.496, three_quarter 0.467, day_1_5 0.239**;
  doy180-200 crash to 0.047; doy200-220 0.039; doy220-240 mild bump 0.116;
  doy240-260 crash again 0.013; doy260-280 recovering 0.105; **doy280-300 FALL
  PEAK 1.735 (best of year by far)**; doy300-320 falling off 0.456.
- Fishdope vs pooled fleet ypa correlation: same-day ~+0.28, next-day ~+0.18
  (weak-ish but real). Weight yt_local/yt_coronado (SD-reachable) over yt_all.
  Confirmed again this season: single-day fishdope spikes (local mentions,
  yt_all ticks) have NOT reliably preceded real count breakouts — treat as a
  minor tiebreaker only, counts are the real trigger.
- Budget/PTO pacing: with $1550/10 PTO intact at doy121, still plenty for both
  a possible 120-180 window AND the fall peak. Rough split if 120-180 turns
  real: ~$500-700 there, keep ~$800-1000 + 6-7 PTO for the fall peak (which
  historically pays off ~4x better per trip). Friday departures for
  overnight/day_1_5 save PTO (0 PTO if back Sun/Mon-holiday).

## Season 2 timeline log (condensed)
- Doy1-91: cold La Niña start, ONI -1.6→-1.29, pier temp 1.0-1.6°C colder than
  S1, trips table flat 0.000 through doy91 despite S1 having a real spring
  spike at doy90-100. Fishdope faint uptick doy85-91, not corroborated by
  counts yet.
- Doy91-121 (nightly log, 30 nights): mostly stayed home on flat signal.
  Booked 3 cheap ($150) three_quarter tests on weekends when fishdope+trailing
  ypa looked promising: d100 (yt=1/29, share 0.024 — small hit), d107 (San
  Diego's d106 breakout of 0.172 ypa reversed to 0 next trip — noise), d113
  (fleet-pooled 0.333 on d112 didn't hold on San Diego's actual boat — noise).
  Correctly did NOT chase any of the single-day spikes. By doy121: three_quarter
  ypa 14-day trailing ~0.065-0.085, overnight dead, one day_1_5 outlier
  (Pacific Voyager 24/24 on d113, uncorroborated). Water temp and ONI both
  caught up/reversed relative to S1 by doy110-120 (see MAJOR UPDATE above) —
  this is the new key fact driving the plan going forward.

## Open items
- Boat-level variance within a class not yet analyzed — do this once a real
  signal window opens and there's count history to compare boats on.
- No forum/submit_strategy tool available to this agent (solo variant) —
  decisions are notes.md + nightly briefing judgment only.
